evidence: Original CAP-04.S05.T02 R02 independently approved the signed Windows LPAC restriction, broker denial, cleanup and durable content-free failure audit at 5a76725c. The correction does not change the LPAC worker, guardian, broker, credential, grant validator or human trust/enable authority; original R02 evidence is historical support only for those unchanged boundaries.

At exact candidate 3dde9123, 49 focused dispatch/job/broker/consent tests pass, including changed-host/path/method/scheme denial before egress; the new real Core-admin persisted-dispatch test denies system trust/enable, proves human grant, then reaches one synthetic broker call. That committed regression uses SQLCipher with an in-memory key and real DPAPI publisher trust, not production DPAPI project-key composition. The protected local native preflight reaches signed LPAC and publishes/reopens one page with production DPAPI/SQLCipher, but uses test signing, synthetic HTTP, an overridden runtime-availability gate, and an injected ignored runtime helper without full frozen input closure. S05 two-page, joined denial/cancellation and process-restart proof remains separate.

Both migration tests were red at the clean paused predecessor due to a stale fixture that mixed v20 with successor DDL. The corrected test constructs exact encrypted v20, pins the frozen fingerprint, verifies ordered v21/v22/v23 fingerprints/history, verified backup/reopen, and injected v21 step rollback/retry. Both pass inside the 20-test focused Core group; production DDL is unchanged.

The new regression first failed against the byte-unchanged workload actor after real human trust/enable and before broker egress. At exact candidate it passes through persisted Core authorization using the existing system runtime actor, while system trust/enable remains denied. Overall 20 Core, 9 authority, 49 dispatch and one protected signed native preflight tests pass; red logs and the separate dev-plaintext package-pointer trace remain in ignored artifacts.

The only product/test paths in the exact base-to-candidate diff are the three spec-admitted files: plugin_worker.py and the worker-submission and grant-migration test modules. The remaining five paths are taskctl claim and generated planning views. No approved permission, grant validator, production migration, broker, LPAC, build, UX or audit contract changed.

At clean committed candidate, affected Ruff lint/format and mypy pass, taskctl validates the claim ledger, and fresh focused encrypted migration/denial checks pass. Full joined S05 integration, later checkpoint and W2 exit qualification remain governed separate work.

verificationSelection.riskAnalysis: The one-line product change affects persisted Core grant authorization; the second change repairs a test-only encrypted migration fixture. Focused worker/grant/admin, broker/consent and native signed-LPAC/Core checks target the plausible identity, denial, migration and durable-publication failures. Ruff/mypy cover all three changed paths; taskctl validates the correction claim. The ignored native probe authenticates its selected worker/guardian/sample bytes but overrides source-checkout runtime availability and imports an ignored helper outside a fully frozen input closure; it is only a one-page synthetic preflight. A separate development plaintext Python 3.14 package-pointer transaction failure was preserved and does not reproduce in the protected correction path; it is outside this three-path correction scope.
deferred: S05 slice integration must join signed sample to protected Core for two pages, denial/cancellation and restart/recovery with independent slice review; the one-page preflight does not discharge that obligation.

Unchanged broad service/security-local/desktop/packaging profiles remain checkpoint or fresh W2 exit work under verification §8.1; this correction has no changed worker image, guardian, build or desktop inputs.
Dev-only plaintext package-pointer transaction behavior requires separate triage outside this fixed correction spec.
